question: If the surface areas of two spheres are in the ratio of 4 ∶ 25, then find the ratio of their volumes.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Surface Area Ratio (S₁:S₂) = (Radius Ratio)² = 4 : 25

Radius Ratio (r₁:r₂) = √4 : √25 = 2 : 5

Volume Ratio (V₁:V₂) = (Radius Ratio)³ = 2³ : 5³

Required Ratio = 8 : 125

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of surface areas of two spheres = 4 : 25

**Formula Used:**

Surface area of a sphere = 4 × π × r²

Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

 
 
 
• 
 r₁
 Area = 4k
 
 
 
 
• 
 r₂
 Area = 25k

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the radii of the two spheres be r₁ and r₂.

⇒ (4 × π × r₁²) ÷ (4 × π × r₂²) = 4 ÷ 25

⇒ r₁² ÷ r₂² = 4 ÷ 25

⇒ r₁ ÷ r₂ = √(4 ÷ 25) = 2 ÷ 5

⇒ Volume Ratio = [(4/3) × π × r₁³] ÷ [(4/3) × π × r₂³]

⇒ Volume Ratio = (r₁ ÷ r₂)³

⇒ Volume Ratio = (2 ÷ 5)³ = 8 ÷ 125

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Sphere and Hemisphere

For a sphere of radius r, Surface Area = 4πr² and Volume = (4/3)πr³. For a hemisphere, Curved Surface Area = 2πr² and Total Surface Area = 3πr².

Scaling Rules for 3D Shapes

If the linear dimensions (like radius) are in ratio a:b, then areas are in ratio a²:b² and volumes are in ratio a³:b³. This applies to all similar solids like cubes, spheres, and cylinders.

Direct Relation between Area and Volume

The ratio of volumes of two spheres can be calculated from the ratio of their surface areas (S₁/S₂) using the formula: V₁/V₂ = (S₁/S₂)³/².</p
